'''Otto Helmut Kegel''' ({{IPA|de|ˈɔtoː ˈhɛlmuːt ˈkeːgəl|lang}}; 20 July 1934 – 20 July 2025) was a German mathematician who worked on [[group theory]].  He was a professor at the [[University of Freiburg]].

==Early life and career==
Kegel was born on 20 July 1934 in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deutsche-biographie.de/gnd1095794965.html?language=en| title=Kegel, Otto H. | work=Deutsche Biographie
 |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/zur-person-xra3sf4ix|newspaper=Badische Zeitung|title=Zur Person|date=20 July 2004|access-date=3 August 2025}}</ref>  His parents were German, and the family returned to Germany in 1938.<ref name="jgtmem">{{cite journal | last1=Kuzucuoǧlu |first1= Mahmut | journal=Advances in Group Theory and Applications | title=Otto H. Kegel (1934– 2025) | volume=21 | pages=1–9 | date= 2025 | issn=2499-1287 | doi=10.32037/agta-2025-004}}
</ref>  He attended high school in [[Frankfurt am Main]].<ref name="jgtmem"/>

Kegel received his PhD from [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] in 1961, with a thesis titled ''Vertauschbarkeit von Untergruppen und Kompositionsstruktur in endlichen Gruppen'' (''Commutability of subgroups and composition structure in finite groups'') and supervised by [[Reinhold Baer]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy| 23901 }}</ref><!-- MGP gives also Wolfgang Franz as a second advisor, but other sources list only Baer -->  He completed his habilitation at the same institution in 1966.<ref name="kurschners"/>

In 1962, Kegel gave a talk titled ''Locally finite groups with a partition'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Stockholm]], Sweden.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1962.p/ICM1962.p.ocr.pdf|publisher=International Mathematical Union|year=1962|title=International Congress of Mathematicians {{!}} Programme|access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref>

Kegel started at [[Queen Mary College]] in the [[University of London]] as a reader in 1968, and was promoted to professor in 1970.<ref name="jgtmem"/>  He moved to the [[University of Freiburg]] beginning in 1975, where he worked as a professor until his retirement in 1999.<ref name="jgtmem"/><ref name="kurschners"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bztrauer.de/traueranzeige/92113/prof-otto-kegel | title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Otto H. Kegel | date=31 July 2025 | work=Badische Zeitung | via=BZTrauer | access-date=3 August 2025 }}</ref>  He was an editor for ''[[Archiv der Mathematik]]'' from 1975 until 1990.<ref name="kurschners">{{cite book|title=Kürschners Deutscher Gelehrten-Kalender|year=2009|publisher=K. G. Saur Verlag|isbn=978-3-598-23629-7}}</ref><ref name="archivdedic"/>

==Death==
Kegel died on 20 July 2025, his 91st birthday.<ref name="bzobit">{{cite news|url=https://bztrauer.de/en/memorial/92049/otto-h-kegel| newspaper=Badische Zeitung|via=BZTrauer | date=26 July 2025|title= Otto H. Kegel {{!}} 20 July 1934 - 20 July 2025 | access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref>

==Research==
Kegel worked in the field of group theory, a part of [[abstract algebra]].  His book on [[locally finite group]]s, written with Bertram Wehrfritz, was influential in the subfield.<ref name="jgtmem"/>  [[Prime graph]]s are also known as Gruenberg-Kegel graphs due to early unpublished work of Kegel with [[Karl W. Gruenberg]] on the topic.<ref name="jgtmem"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1985, ''Archiv der Mathematik'' dedicated an issue to Kegel, in honor of his contributions to the journal as an author, editor, and on the advisory board.<ref name="archivdedic">{{cite journal|title= Dedication to Prof. Dr. Otto H. Kegel |journal=Archiv der Mathematik|year=1985|volume=85|issue=1|pages=1–2|doi= 10.1007/s00013-005-0009-y }}</ref>  A conference ''Algebra and Group Theory'' was held in Kegel's honor at the [[University of Upper Alsace]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lmia.uha.fr/conf-kegel/Kegeliweb/Home.html|title=Conference: Algebra and Group Theory|publisher=University of Upper Alsace|access-date=27 July 2025}}</ref>  The 2024 edition of the Ischia Group Theory conference was also dedicated to Kegel, marking his 90th birthday.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/unisa.it/igt|title=Ischia Group Theory 2024 (conference homepage) | access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref>
